page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the ESv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. This server is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory performance, with a PassMark memory score of 2894.78 and a large-block write memory bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Read-only memory bandwidth reaches 1259.92 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 166.41 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. CPU performance remains average, with a PassMark CPU score of 30451.25 and a single-core Geekbench score of 1712.0. The server handles database operations at an average rate of 12292.13 PassMark database operations and processes Redis SET operations at 23.93 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the E96-24s_v5 is the complete lack of local storage and GPU accelerators, meaning all storage needs must be met via external Premium Storage. This configuration offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive local disk I/O or parallel GPU processing. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise applications, data caching layers, and memory-heavy analytical workloads.
